questions.stem:
Statements: W > P < T > X < U.
Conclusions: I. U ≤ T   II. W ≥ P.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: No coins is a deposits. Some deposits are tokens. All tokens are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are bonds.
II. Some bonds are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are deposits. Some deposits are tokens. All tokens are bonds.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are bonds.
II. No deposits is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are deposits. All deposits are tokens. No tokens is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some coins are deposits. All deposits are tokens. No tokens is a bonds.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are tokens.
II. Some deposits are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 51 km west, turns right and walks 56 km, then turns right and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 70. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 42 km along the initial direction and 56 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(42² + 56²) = 70 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 64 km north, turns left and walks 105 km, then turns left and walks 8 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 119. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 56 km along the initial direction and 105 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(56² + 105²) = 119 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 71 km east, turns left and walks 120 km, then turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 136. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 64 km along the initial direction and 120 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(64² + 120²) = 136 km.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural banking access = pa vo ze
rural growth digital = to mi pa
banking growth credit = vo mi su
access digital credit = to su ze
rural banking credit = vo su pa
What is the code for “access”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ze. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = pa, banking = vo, access = ze, growth = mi, digital = to, credit = su.

questions.stem: In a queue of 40 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. New front rank = 8+3 = 11. Back rank = 40 − 11 + 1 = 30.

questions.stem: In a queue of 38 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. New front rank = 17+4 = 21. Back rank = 38 − 21 + 1 = 18.

questions.stem: C is the brother of G. G is the mother of A. F is the father of C and G. How is C related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of A’s mother G. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the mother of C. A is the son of C. G is the father of C. How is A related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. G is a parent of C, and A is C’s son. Hence A is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of H. H is the father of G. D is the son of G. C is the sister of H. How is H related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. H is the father of G, and G is D’s mother. Thus H is the maternal grandfather.
